Its ONLY writers are engine.js:4731 setTimeOfDay (harness verb), engine.js:4465/7118 (rest/advanceTime), and save/state.js:748 (load). This is exactly the RI-MTH07 pattern the brief named: a model whose only writer is a harness verb. There is no day/night CYCLE in the build.

No transition machine, no per-region weather selection, nothing reads regions.json .weather[] at runtime. render/sky.js's own comment says 'W1-02 owns the transition machine' - it was left for me.

GOOD NEWS - the downstream consumers are REAL and behavioural, so a clock/weather that moves will be demonstrable: sim/stealth/system.js:880-881 reads env.timeOfDay AND env.weather for detection; sim/souls.js:81-96 awards differently at night; sim/npc.js:147 picks a schedule slot from env.timeOfDay; sim/settlement.js:243 opens doors by hour; sim/hazards.js:154 stamps weather/hour. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED in stealth: sim/stealth/system.js skyAmbient() classified only 3 weather ids as overcast ('overcast','storm','rain') out of the 20 render/sky.js already declared. heavy_rain, salt_storm, fever_fog, sea_squall, ashfall and every regional state were lit as MIDDAY SUN (ambient 1.00) by the stealth model while the renderer drew a black sky - the two halves of the build were looking at different weather. SECOND MODEL DEFECT, found by my own probe and fixed: sky.js was combining the region's fog extinction with the weather's by Math.max(). In the four regions whose own extinction is already high (blackwood 0.018/m, hive, marauders-coast, stone-forest) the region term beat EVERY state its machine can roll, so weather changed the frame by exactly nothing in 4 of 13 regions - RI-WLD08's 'weather as a colour grade' arriving through a Math.max. Extinction coefficients add; now additive, and all 13 regions show 4 distinct realised sightlines.

THIRD PROBE DEFECT, self-caught: the first C2 called awardFor('str', h) - awardFor takes a STATBLOCK and returns souls 0 for anything with no .souls field, so the check passed vacuously against a placeholder. Rewritten against a real stat and a hour inside RI-PRG04's 21:00-05:00 window.

THREE INSTRUMENT DEFECTS FOUND BY RUNNING THE TRAVERSE AGAINST THE LIVE FIELD RATHER THAN THE DECLARED OFFSETS - each would have shipped a wrong number: (1) the signed distance raster is 25 m/cell, so nearest-neighbour reads made nine crossovers 5.5 m apart land in the SAME cell - 23 of 24 borders had 5-6 axis pairs inside the 3 m limit while the data was correct. Fixed by bilinear interpolation, which also stopped the ground colour changing in 25 m squares. (2) anchoring the traverse at the border's NARROWEST point put it where the distance band is thinnest, so the walk left the band before the early axes handed over and every axis flipped together at the raster line - a perfect texture swap on 3 of 24 from a correct build. (3) a STRAIGHT perpendicular is perpendicular only where it was fitted; on a curving frontier arc length and signed distance come apart and the ruler bends. The walk now follows the gradient at every step.

notes_for_successor: WHAT IS BUILT AND MEASURED - do not rebuild any of it: the 20x clock in the fixed step (259,200 frames/game day), the 13 per-region weather machines (41 states, RI-WLD08 §5), the border field (24 borders, staggered nine-axis crossover, 8 threshold-object types, 7 announced tier jumps), and four instruments (env-consumption 9/9, border-traverse 24/24, wld-env-live 6/6 in the browser, wld12-blind-pack). || THE BIGGEST THING I DID NOT DO IS HEIGHT FOG, and W1-01-r4's handover is right that it is the highest-value remaining identity lever: regions.json declares fog.height_falloff_m 45-340 m per region and render/sky.js still reads none of it (FogExp2 has no height term). Their colour-stripped measurement says the VERTICAL LUMINANCE PROFILE is the only half of the descriptor that carries signal (lum-only Fisher 1.528 vs edge-only 0.987). It needs a THREE.ShaderChunk patch to fog_pars_vertex/fog_vertex/fog_fragment plus two uniforms merged into THREE.UniformsLib.fog before any material is created, and then a full recapture. I did not attempt it because it touches every material in the build and the tree was being rewritten under me by other agents all afternoon; a half-applied shader patch is a black province. || WHAT ELSE IS OPEN. (a) RI-WLD12 M66 T2 - 'first hostile encounter beyond a tier border >= 40 m' - is DECLARED in borders.json as first_hostile_min_m and is NOT enforced by the encounter system; someone must wire it or a critic will correctly score it unmeasured. (b) The threshold objects are placed in DATA (210 of them, 8 types) but have no MESH: world/signature.js has geometry for the 13 only-here kinds and nothing for cairns, root-gates, tide-poles or the corpse in a cage, so M68's '>= 70% name an object' cannot pass until they are drawn. That is the single highest-value next build step for this path and it is a rendering job, not a data one. (c) marauders-coast--western-rootlands resolves only 6 of 9 axes in a 400 m traverse. (d) RI-WLD04 and RI-WLD05 judge only LEGACY path names and judge none of W1-02's declared paths - worth a corpus amendment. || THE BLIND PACK IS BUILT BUT NOT RUN: tools/world/wld12-blind-pack.mjs. It shuffles (deterministic Fisher-Yates, seed 0xb11d, re-derivable), names frames f00.png.. and writes the answer key to a separate KEY.json. DO NOT JUDGE IT YOURSELF - the brief and RI-MTH03 both forbid it and it has voided two comparisons already.
